title: Remco Evenepoel calls Jonas Vingegaard’s help ‘amazing’ in tense Volta a Catalunya stage
content:
Remco Evenepoel said cooperation with breakaway partner Jonas Vingegaard was “amazing” in a sarcastic response to a tense end of the Volta a Catalunya’s third stage.

The Belgian had put in a strong solo effort to hold off the peloton once he realised that Vingegaard was not going to take a turn on the front inside the final five kilometers, before crashing only 500m before the finish.

The Dane continued over the final roundabout but did not contest the sprint, leaving INEOS Grenadiers rider Dorian Godon to take his second win of the week and retain the leader’s jersey.

“I wanted to go to my drops for the sprint, and right at that moment there was quite a big hole,” Evenepoel said. “I hit it. I didn’t see it, and it was also not very clear on the road, no markings or anything. I just didn’t see it and lost my bars.

“I think there are some bigger injuries, so we’ll have to see tonight and tomorrow morning how everything reacts. But like I said, I’m still standing, nothing is broken, so that’s positive.”

Evenepoel had appeared frustrated with Vingegaard’s lack of cooperation in the closing stages, gesticulating with his hand before deciding to take matters into his own hands. When asked about it after the race, he was deadpan, saying “cooperation was amazing”.

“He went, I went jumped across. I was happy I could do that,” Vingegaard said. “Yes, Remco wasn’t happy with me at some point today, but that’s cycling, that’s how it is.”

“I don’t know how Remco crashed,” the Visma-Lease a Bike rider continued. “He just flew over his handlebars; it looked crazy. I didn’t want to take advantage of that, so I waited for the bunch. I hope he’s OK.”

With the stage billed as a bunch sprint, the times were neutralised after the 5km mark so Evenepoel stays second in the general classification, 11 seconds behind Godon. Vingegaard sits fourth in the GC, seven seconds behind the Red Bull Bora Hansgrohe rider and two behind Tom Pidcock in third.

Stage four of the WorldTour race on Thursday was set to be a mountain-top finish at the Vallter ski resort, but was shortened on Wednesday evening due to expected high winds, taking out the final climb to the finish and concluding in Camprodon.
